arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Mooppan argued for the board members. He stated that public officials remain private citizens. He claimed they retain First Amendment rights on personal property.
Mr. Joshi argued for the critics. He agreed that duty and authority determine capacity. He urged the Court to focus on property access denials.
Ms. Karlan argued for the critics. She cited the district court finding. She noted that receiving feedback is part of the trustees' duties.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: School board members blocked critics on a personal Facebook page. Critics sued under federal civil rights law. The lower court ruled the board acted as state officials. The board members seek reversal.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: The board members want the Court to rule that personal social media posts are private speech. They seek to dismiss the civil rights lawsuit.
The critics want the Court to rule that the board members acted as state officials. They seek to keep the civil rights lawsuit alive.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: The board members argue they retain First Amendment rights when acting in a personal capacity. They claim they can decide who participates in their own community discussions.
The critics argue the board members had a duty to receive constituent feedback. They claim the board controlled the platform and acted as state officials.
